record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: Nies, Schlicht, and Tent showed that topological isomorphism of oligomorphic groups is Borel reducible to E_∞. Is that isomorphism relation actually smooth?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Nies, Schlicht, and Tent proved in 2019 [2] that the topological isomorphism of oligomorphic groups is ≤B E∞. Is it smooth?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S_\infty$ denote the Polish group of all permutations of $\mathbb{N}$ with the pointwise convergence topology. A closed subgroup $G \le S_\infty$ is called oligomorphic if for every $n \ge 1$ the natural action of $G$ on $\mathbb{N}^n$ has only finitely many orbits. The space of closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ is a standard Borel space, on which topological isomorphism $\cong_{\mathrm{top}}$ is an analytic equivalence relation.

Given Borel equivalence relations $E, F$ on standard Borel spaces $X, Y$, one says $E$ is Borel reducible to $F$, written $E \le_B F$, if there exists a Borel map $f : X \to Y$ such that $x \mathrel{E} x'$ iff $f(x) \mathrel{F} f(x')$. An equivalence relation $E$ is called smooth if $E \le_B \mathrm{id}_{\mathbb{R}}$ (equivalently, classes can be separated by a Borel function into a standard Borel space). The equivalence relation $E_\infty$ is the universal countable Borel equivalence relation, i.e., the $\le_B$-maximum among Borel equivalence relations all of whose classes are countable.

It is known that the restriction of $\cong_{\mathrm{top}}$ to oligomorphic closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ is Borel reducible to $E_\infty$. Determine whether this restricted topological isomorphism relation on oligomorphic closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ is smooth.
artifact.status_search_result: The Nies–Schlicht–Tent result (2019/2021) establishes that topological isomorphism of oligomorphic closed subgroups of $S_\infty$ is Borel reducible to a countable Borel equivalence relation (hence to $E_\infty$). Subsequent literature, including Kechris–Nies–Tent, leaves open whether this relation is smooth; no later source found that resolves the question.

status_evidence.title: Coarse groups, and the isomorphism problem for oligomorphic groups
status_evidence.snippet: The isomorphism relation for oligomorphic subgroups of S∞ is Borel reducible to a Borel equivalence relation with all classes countable.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the ≤_B E_∞ upper bound; smoothness is not claimed.

status_evidence.title: The complexity of topological group isomorphism
status_evidence.snippet: Studies complexity of topological isomorphism of closed subgroups of S∞.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work that does not establish smoothness for oligomorphic groups.
